problems.problem: BLOCKING (proven live). abort() releases the held POST with `{done:true, result:{cancelled:true}}` — the SAME decision finish() sends. I drove this in a headless browser: after abort() the page renders a green check and 'Done. You can close this tab.' Every failure between two stops therefore tells the user the setup succeeded. The most common one is real and one line away: capyCommand.ts:481 throws 'You have access to "<org>" but no encryption key on this device' for any invited teammate, initializeProject catches it, calls wizard.abort(), and the browser says Done. The init-wizard contract has a `blocked: Blocked` + `blockedNames` field for exactly this state and it is never used. The code comment claims abort exists 'so the page stops claiming to be working on something that has already stopped' — it now claims something strictly worse than 'working'.

BLOCKING (proven live). runBrowserWizard's timer is a single whole-session wall clock set once at listen() and never reset on activity (browserWizard.ts:~270; the module header calls it 'an idle timeout' — it is not). Before this change each selectInBrowser/promptTextInBrowser call stood up its own server and got a fresh 5-minute budget PER QUESTION. 'One window, not seven' now puts the entire first run under one 5-minute budget, and InitWizardSession never passes a timeoutMs, so it takes DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS. That budget starts at the organization stop and must also cover createNewOrganization (capyCommand.ts:2163 -> orgCreation.ts), which under --web opens two MORE browser windows: naming the org (with a network availability check and retries on a taken name) and showRecoveryPhraseInBrowser, where the user is asked to write down 24 words and confirm them. Writing down a 24-word phrase alone plausibly exceeds five minutes. I reproduced the mechanism with timeoutMs 2000 and 2.5s of work between two stops: the second ask() throws. Failure mode: the org exists, the master key is minted and the phrase has been shown ONCE, and then the run dies with `Error: The setup window has already closed.` — a bare Error with no CapyError code.

MAJOR (proven live) — a false security claim with a test that appears to check it and does not. The file header states 'Values never appear in either payload... the comparison itself is done on 16-hex sha256 prefixes and not even those cross.' statusCommand.ts builds `report` whose `diffs` are the raw compareSecrets rows (pinned/local/remote sha256 prefixes) and passes `json: JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)` straight into the payload. I loaded the page in a real browser with the REAL json shape: the hash string is present in document.body.textContent. The parcel's own browser test asserts `!body.textContent.includes('a1b2c3d4e5f60718')` and only passes because its fixture's `json` is a stub `{projectName, inSync}` with no diffs — so the one assertion that looks like it guards the payload is vacuous. Not a plaintext-secret leak (the same hashes already go to stdout under `capy status --json`), but the comment is wrong and the test proves nothing.

MAJOR. `capy status --web` is dead code. index.ts:113-117 constructs StatusCommand and calls `execute({ json: options.json })` — `web` is never passed, and `--web` is a global on the root program so the subcommand's own `options.web` is undefined. Verified by running the built binary: `node dist/index.js status --web` prints the TTY output. One of the four screens assigned to this parcel (`sync-status`) ships unreachable, along with its whole --web branch in statusCommand. The agent reported this accurately and the fix (the `optsWithGlobals().web` pattern already at index.ts:418) is outside the parcel — but the parcel is not done for that screen. index-dev.ts:278-282 has the same gap.

MAJOR. reportSyncResult now fires on the 'Everything is up to date!' no-op path (line 1494) as well as the three real ends, so `capy --web` opens a browser tab and serves a report on EVERY run. ScreenServer holds a ref'd listening socket until the page is fetched (closes 250ms later) or its 120s timeout expires. `open()` is best-effort and swallows failure ('the URL is printed above'), so on a headless or remote host — which is the normal --web/MCP situation — every no-op sync now ends in a 120-second hang instead of printing one line and exiting.

MINOR. askBranchName validates with branchNameProblem(name, []) from the checkout parcel, which additionally refuses whitespace and a leading hyphen. The TTY prompt this replaces validated only `input.trim().length > 0`. `--web` and the terminal therefore accept different first-branch names — that is a change of LOGIC, not of rendering, which the brief forbids. (Not a dead end: I confirmed in the browser that the screen holds its 'Create branch' button on a name with a space, so the server refusal is only a backstop.)

MINOR — coverage gap on the refusal path. The wizard has five inline `{error:'…'}` refusals (unreachable org, foreign project, both name validators, the encrypt gate). No browser test in this repo drives a CLI-side `{error}` against a STANDALONE compiled screen — the one test that covers inline refusal (line 155) uses the wizard shell and asserts on `document.getElementById('status')`, which a compiled screen does not have. Also `InitWizardView.rejected` / `data.rejected` is built by buildInitWizardData and exercised only by a unit test; nothing in production ever sets it.

MINOR. unansweredInitStops is exported and referenced only by its own test. The partition's done-criterion #2 says the stops array is 'what --json emits', but the root `capy` command has no --json, so there is no headless consumer. Dead production code.

MINOR (regression in the branch picker). The old --web path passed `defaultId: defaultName` — the CLI's recommended branch, computed by selectBranchWithServer and deliberately never a protected branch. chooseBranchInBrowser has no field for it, so under --web the recommendation is now dropped entirely. Reported by the agent as a packages/ui shape change; confirming it is a real behaviour loss today, not just a wording nit.
